reference: No matching GNU CLI exists for Bash's array builtin. Operation expectations are fixed independently from the stock Bash asort help contract and documented semantics; C-locale lexical order and distinct numeric values give explicit expected arrays. These are contract checks, not GNU parity comparisons.
coverage: Bash type/help metadata and documented option synopsis
In-place lexical sorting, including sparse-index compaction
Reverse sorting across multiple indexed arrays
Indexed destination mode with sparse source indexes, including numeric mode
Associative source keys ordered by their values
Empty arrays and documented error/usage statuses
Failures remain nonzero while later valid arrays are sorted and rejected variables stay unchanged.
Empty/space-bearing strings and flag reset across repeated calls.
exclusions: No GNU CLI exposes this Bash array API, so no parity cases are claimed.
Equal-key stability is not documented and is intentionally not asserted.
Locale-sensitive non-ASCII collation, malformed numeric strings, and large-array performance are outside this small deterministic suite.
Error wording is allowed to vary; error cases assert status and nonempty stderr.
In-place sorting of associative arrays is excluded because the documented contract forbids it and this suite does not probe that unsupported operation.

cases.purpose: Check Bash reports asort as a builtin and help exposes its summary, numeric option, index-mode description, and associative-array restriction.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t asort) == builtin ]]
help_text=$(help asort)
[[ $help_text == *"Sort arrays in-place."* ]]
[[ $help_text == *"-n  compare according to string numerical value"* ]]
[[ $help_text == *"SOURCE is not sorted in-place"* ]]
[[ $help_text == *"Associative arrays may not be sorted in-place."* ]]
printf '%s\n' 'builtin-help-ok'

cases.purpose: Sort sparse indexed values by C-locale lexical order and verify in-place sorting renumbers elements densely from zero.
Check -r reverses lexical order and applies to every indexed array named in one invocation.
cases.script:
left=(pear apple fig)
right=(delta beta gamma)
asort -r left right
printf 'left=%s\nright=%s\n' "${left[*]}" "${right[*]}"
cases.stdout:
left=pear fig apple
right=gamma delta beta

cases.purpose: Sort distinct negative, fractional, and integral numeric strings in ascending numeric order with -n.
Check combined -nr options produce descending numeric order for distinct values.
Sort an indexed source by its values, place original sparse indexes in a dense destination, and leave source values unchanged.
For an associative source, sort by values and emit the corresponding keys in an indexed destination without modifying the source.
cases.script:
declare -A colors=([violet]=plum [green]=leaf [red]=apple)
asort -i keys colors
printf 'keys=%s\nsource=%s %s %s\n' "${keys[*]}" "${colors[red]}" "${colors[green]}" "${colors[violet]}"
cases.stdout:
keys=red green violet
source=apple leaf plum

cases.purpose: Combine -n and -i to emit sparse indexed keys in the order of their distinct numeric source values.
Verify an empty indexed array is a successful no-op and remains empty.
Assert documented failure statuses for a scalar and a readonly indexed array. Diagnostics may vary; unsupported in-place associative sorting is excluded.
cases.script:
scalar=value
declare -ar locked=(z a)
set +e
asort scalar; scalar_rc=$?
asort locked; readonly_rc=$?
set -e
printf 'scalar=%s readonly=%s\n' "$scalar_rc" "$readonly_rc"

cases.purpose: Check usage errors for a missing operand, an unknown option, and incorrect -i arity return the documented usage status.
cases.script:
values=(b a)
if asort; then missing_rc=0; else missing_rc=$?; fi
if asort -z values; then option_rc=0; else option_rc=$?; fi
if asort -i only_destination; then index_rc=0; else index_rc=$?; fi
printf 'missing=%s option=%s index-arity=%s\n' "$missing_rc" "$option_rc" "$index_rc"

cases.purpose: An earlier rejected scalar or readonly array must keep the command status nonzero even when later valid arrays sort successfully; rejected values stay intact.
cases.script:
declare -a left=(z a) right=(d b)
scalar=value
declare -ar locked=(y x)
rc=0
asort left scalar locked right || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
printf "status=%s left=%s,%s right=%s,%s scalar=%s locked=%s,%s\n" "$rc" "${left[0]}" "${left[1]}" "${right[0]}" "${right[1]}" "$scalar" "${locked[0]}" "${locked[1]}"

cases.purpose: Sort empty and whitespace-bearing strings without splitting or dropping values.
cases.script:
values=('z z' '' 'a b' a)
asort values
printf '<%s>\n' "${values[@]}"

cases.purpose: Numeric/reverse flags must reset before a later default lexical invocation.
cases.script:
first=(2 10 1); second=(2 10 1)
asort -nr first
asort second
printf '%s\n' "${first[*]}" "${second[*]}"
